purpose: Give living-language speakers and source communities effective authority to contest, suspend, revise, or remove Caeluviim uses of their language.

principles.living_authority: A language is not merely a lexical resource. Living speakers and communities retain interpretive and relational authority that a protocol adoption cannot supersede.
principles.presumptive_standing: Any self-identified speaker of the source language has presumptive standing to contest a Caeluviim lexical form, gloss, semantic extension, rendering, provenance statement, or use condition. No academic credential, institutional office, or formal community title is required to initiate contestation.
principles.burden_allocation: Once a good-faith objection is raised, Caeluviim bears the burden of justifying continued active use. The speaker is not required to prove ownership of the language or demonstrate measurable harm.
principles.nonappropriation: Protocol use does not create ownership, authority over the language, or a right to continue use against speaker or community objection.
principles.plurality: Disagreement among speakers must be represented as disagreement. Caeluviim must not invent a singular community consensus where none is established.

eligible_contestants: a language teacher, translator, elder, cultural worker, or knowledge keeper
a tribal, community, educational, or language-revitalization body
another person transmitting a documented objection from an eligible contestant
eligible_grounds: harmful, disrespectful, extractive, or unwanted use
objection to active protocol adoption itself
contestation_process.immediate_effect: A facially good-faith objection marks the entry CONTESTED. When the objection concerns misrepresentation, cultural harm, or unwanted use, active generation and new deployment of the challenged form are suspended pending disposition.
contestation_process.verification_rule: Verification is limited to determining that the objection plausibly originates from a speaker or source-community participant. It must not become a burdensome credentialing process or a test of whether the objection is sufficiently academic.
contestation_process.review_rule: Review must preserve the contestant's own words where permission allows, identify conflicting evidence or speaker views, and avoid substituting non-speaker institutional authority for living-language testimony.
contestation_process.time_rule: A suspended entry remains inactive until disposition. Delay does not silently restore active use.

available_dispositions.effect: Correct spelling, grammar, gloss, scope, provenance, or rendering while retaining the decision history.
Restrict the protocol use to a speaker-supported semantic or contextual scope.
Select another lexeme or language anchor and deprecate the contested entry.
Remove the lexeme from active protocol use and all default renderings.
Preserve the entry only as a historical or research record with the objection prominently attached; it is not an active protocol term.

removal_semantics.active_removal: Removal means the word is no longer emitted, recommended, mapped as canonical, or presented as an operative Caeluviim term.
removal_semantics.provenance_preservation: The repository retains a tombstoned decision record showing the former use, objection, disposition, and date. Historical retention is not continued active use.
removal_semantics.downstream_repair: Caeluviim must identify and update dependent schemas, ontologies, documentation, examples, prompts, and generated artifacts where practicable.
removal_semantics.no_retaliation: A contestant's objection must not diminish their standing, be characterized as obstruction, or be used to appropriate additional personal or community information.

initial_application.rule: Any Anishinaabemowin speaker or source-community participant may contest the spelling, gloss, protocol extension, first-recovered-word framing, or use of Anishinaabe as the Caeluviim term for Person. A validated objection may revise, replace, or remove the term from active protocol use.

initiating_authority: User instruction on 2026-08-06: if speakers contest a protocol use, they can have it removed.
